cancellation.fcmaes.evaluate/1: between points; Scalar::simulation models also at SimContext checkpoints
cancellation.fcmaes.map-elites/1: between generations; the run returns what it has
cancellation.fcmaes.mode/1: between generations; the run returns what it has
cancellation.fcmaes.retry/1: between retries; active retries run until their budget or process deadline; Scalar::simulation models stop at SimContext checkpoints, and the rest of the retry's evaluations return +inf at once
cancellation.fcmaes.surrogate/1: stop before proposals and evaluations; Scalar::simulation also stops at SimContext checkpoints; plain callbacks must finish or the runner enforces the process deadline

claims.best_found: fcmaes.retry/1 and fcmaes.surrogate/1: best evaluated point, no global certificate; surrogate evidence is rechecked only after exact independent deterministic re-evaluation, otherwise claimed; warm values remain historical inputs; a cancelled Scalar::simulation retry's point is not rechecked (claimed)
claims.elite_archive: fcmaes.map-elites/1: every elite in details.elites is re-evaluated and maps to its niche; x/objective are the best elite; evidence rechecked [objective, bounds, niche]
claims.feasible: scalar and quality-diversity models (fcmaes.evaluate/1; fcmaes.retry/1 and fcmaes.surrogate/1 after an objective_mismatch refutation): within bounds and a usable value; no constraint check (they declare no constraints; a penalty inside the objective is not checked). Multi-objective models (fcmaes.evaluate/1): every declared constraint <= 0, rechecked
claims.non_dominated_set: fcmaes.mode/1: details.front is the feasible non-dominated part of the final population, re-evaluated; evidence rechecked; no Pareto-optimality certificate
claims.none: no usable answer (claimed evidence: a penalty value, a failed simulation, an empty front or archive); with evidence.refuted, a best_found claim that failed its re-check

evaluation.points: 1 or more points (inline: the resolved job, points included, must stay below the runner's 4 MiB validation output), each of the problem's dimension and inside its bounds; one task per point
evaluation.problems: every registered model, Scalar::simulation models included
evaluation.result: claim feasible: a scalar or quality-diversity model gave a usable value at a point inside the bounds; such models declare no constraints, so a penalty inside the objective is not checked (details.constraints says so); a multi-objective model: every declared constraint <= 0; objectives, constraints or descriptor in details
evaluation.run_seed: optional, simulation models only: a retry's or surrogate run's details.run_seed re-evaluates its points with the same point seeds
evaluation.simulation: Scalar::simulation models get a SimContext with threads() 1, the seed derived from run_seed (default 0) and the point, the remaining time and the job's cancellation; a failed evaluation gives claim none with details.error; a cancelled one termination cancelled

description.execution: native registered models; no deserialized callbacks

fcmaes.surrogate.observations/1.$comment: the surrogate-observations-TASK artifact of an earlier job; its problem must equal the new job's resolved model identity (parameters with defaults, SHA-256 of the model inputs, simulation run seed); observation ids are unique and each x has dimension values

description.inputs: model inputs are hash-checked and must be consumed; fcmaes.surrogate/1 may additionally consume its named warm-start input

optimizers.best: every optimizer reports the best point it evaluated; for CR-FM-NES and PGPE it is tracked from the evaluated populations

biteopt.batch: optional, 1..1000000 (batch * dimension <= 1e7): ask, evaluate and tell batches of this many candidates (delayed feedback); absent: the serial algorithm of fcmaes.job/0.1
biteopt.inner_threads: 1 without batch; with batch, evaluates each batch on inner_threads threads

ranges.population: 4..1000000; population * dimension <= 1e7 (the default exceeds it from dimension 1825 on)

biteopt.start: without guess: BiteOpt's own initial population around the box centre (the serial run is that of fcmaes.job/0.1); guess: a population member, the others Gaussian around it with a quarter of each range

defaults.max_population: with restarts: 512 * population, at most 1e6 and 1e7 / dimension

cmaes.inner_threads: evaluates each population on inner_threads threads
cmaes.restarts: none | ipop (double the population after every stop) | bipop (alternate doubled populations with small populations and step sizes); runs restart until the retry's budget is spent, each from a new uniform random point (also with guess)
cmaes.sigma: initial step size in the normalized [-1,1] box, (0,2]
cmaes.start: guess, or a uniform random point in the bounds from the retry seed; initial step size sigma

crfmnes.inner_threads: evaluates each population on inner_threads threads
crfmnes.start: guess, or a uniform random point in the bounds from the retry seed; initial step size sigma

de.batch: optional, 1..1000000 (batch * dimension <= 1e7): candidates in flight, the delayed update of the Python fcmaes de.minimize(workers=batch); when the oldest is evaluated it is told and one new candidate is asked; results are told in ask order and a batch run spends at most evaluations_per_retry
de.inner_threads: 1 without batch; with batch, evaluates the candidates in flight on inner_threads threads
de.start: without guess: uniform samples in the bounds (the serial run is that of fcmaes.job/0.1); guess: initial and replacement members are normal samples around it with standard deviation sigma in the normalized [-1,1] box, clamped to the bounds

optimizers.guess: optional payload field: the problem's dimension of numbers inside its bounds; every retry starts there (different seeds still make retries differ)

archive.kind: grid (two-dimensional descriptors, the default for them) or cvt (any descriptor dimension, the default otherwise)
archive.samples_per_niche: cvt: uniform samples per niche of the k-means tessellation, default 20; capacity * samples_per_niche <= 1e6 and capacity^2 * samples_per_niche * descriptor dimension <= 1e9
archive.seed: cvt: seed of the tessellation, default the job seed; every run of a job shares its niches

emitter.cma_mae: CMA-MAE (Fontaine and Nikolaidis 2023): fitness - niche threshold; a lower fitness moves the threshold by archive_learning_rate
emitter.cma_me: CMA-ME improvement ranking (Fontaine et al. 2020): candidates filling an empty niche first (by fitness), then those beating their elite (by fitness - elite), then the rest
emitter.restart: from a random elite when CMA-ES stops or a generation improves nothing

map_elites.generations: SBX or Iso+LineDD generations first, then cma_generations; one of them positive
map_elites.inner_threads: evaluates each generation on inner_threads threads
map_elites.limit: exact: generations * chunk_size + cma_generations * emitters * population per run
map_elites.result: re-evaluated elites with niche, fitness, descriptor and visits; coverage and qd_score

mode.hypervolume: exact through four objectives (method exact); above four a deterministic Monte Carlo estimate (method monte_carlo, with samples, seed and standard_error)
mode.inner_threads: evaluates each population on inner_threads threads
mode.reference_point: required unless the model defines one
mode.result: feasible non-dominated final population members, re-evaluated, with their hypervolume

pgpe.inner_threads: evaluates each population on inner_threads threads
pgpe.start: guess, or a uniform random point in the bounds from the retry seed; initial standard deviation sigma

optimizers.simulation: Scalar::simulation models: SimContext with threads() 1, a seed from the retry's run_seed and the point, the remaining time and the job's cancellation; a failed evaluation is +inf, counted in work and details (failed_evaluations, failures); after a cancel, evaluations return +inf without calling the model (cancelled_evaluations, termination cancelled) and the best point is not rechecked (evidence claimed)

fcmaes.evaluate/1.$comment: inner_threads 1, one task per point; every point has one value per variable inside the bounds; run_seed only for Scalar::simulation models (problems: simulation true).

problem.$comment: a registered model with its version and the dimensions its problems entry accepts; bounds: one value per variable (broadcast: one for all), finite, lower < upper, inside the model's domain; parameters: the model's parameters_schema

fcmaes.map-elites/1.$comment: archive.kind defaults to grid for two-dimensional descriptors (problems: descriptor_bounds) and to cvt otherwise; a grid needs two-dimensional descriptors and takes no samples_per_niche or seed. capacity, chunk_size and emitters times population, each times dimension, <= 1e7; emitters times dimension^2 <= 1e7; cvt: capacity times samples_per_niche <= 1e6 and capacity^2 times samples_per_niche times descriptor dimension <= 1e9; 1..100 descriptor dimensions. inner_threads: the threads evaluating a generation (results do not depend on them).

problem.$comment: a registered model with its version and the dimensions its problems entry accepts; bounds: one value per variable (broadcast: one for all), finite, lower < upper, inside the model's domain; parameters: the model's parameters_schema

fcmaes.mode/1.$comment: population <= 1000 for models with three or more objectives (problems: objectives) and population times dimension <= 1e7; reference_point: one value per objective, required unless the model's problems entry has one; inner_threads: the threads evaluating a population (results do not depend on them); generations times population times runs must not overflow.

problem.$comment: a registered model with its version and the dimensions its problems entry accepts; bounds: one value per variable (broadcast: one for all), finite, lower < upper, inside the model's domain; parameters: the model's parameters_schema

fcmaes.retry/1.$comment: inner_threads: 1 for biteopt and de without parameters.batch, otherwise the threads evaluating a population (results do not depend on them). population, batch and (with restarts) max_population times dimension <= 1e7; cmaes: dimension <= 3162 and max_population >= population. guess: one value per variable inside the bounds. de: sigma only with a guess. retries times the per-retry maximum must not overflow.

problem.$comment: a registered model with its version and the dimensions its problems entry accepts; bounds: one value per variable (broadcast: one for all), finite, lower < upper, inside the model's domain; parameters: the model's parameters_schema

fcmaes.surrogate/1.$comment: concurrent times evaluation_threads <= inner_threads <= 8; log_scale is empty or has one entry per variable, and a log-scaled variable needs a positive lower bound; evaluations plus warm-start observations <= 256; warm_start.input names an envelope input in the format fcmaes.surrogate.observations/1 (input_schemas) for the same model, parameters, model inputs and, for simulation models, run seed; gtop models default to failure_threshold 1e10.

problem.$comment: a registered model with its version and the dimensions its problems entry accepts; bounds: one value per variable (broadcast: one for all), finite, lower < upper, inside the model's domain; parameters: the model's parameters_schema

artifacts.surrogate-TASK: records (file surrogate-TASK.jsonl): the evaluation trace, a header, then every start, proposal, completion, cancellation and recheck; readable in pages while the job runs
artifacts.surrogate-observations-TASK: json (file surrogate-observations-TASK.json): the compact observations snapshot, replaced after every completion; the warm_start input of a later job

surrogate.budget: evaluations counts new optimization callbacks; optional final independent callback is validation_evaluations
surrogate.design: centre plus seeded maximin Latin hypercube; one trust region without Thompson sampling or local-data restarts; no Sobol, asynchronous or noisy support in this release
surrogate.method: exact GP: matern52 or rbf, ARD MAP by bounded L-BFGS with analytic gradients; analytic LogEI or minimization LCB with coordinate refinement; TuRBO-style trust region for two of three proposals (trust_region, default true); synchronous Kriging believer
surrogate.scope: deterministic scalar box models, 1..32 variables, new plus reused observations <=256, concurrent 1..8
surrogate.simulation: Scalar::simulation receives SimContext: checkpoint, remaining_seconds, threads and stable point seed; currently supported by this profile only
surrogate.warm_start: a named hashed compact observations JSON file; matching model id/version/dimension/parameters and model-input hashes; new job, no solver resume

claims.feasible: a re-evaluated candidate within the tolerances, without an optimality claim
claims.infeasible: native infeasibility claim (claimed; checked internally with a Farkas row, which is not exported); refuted by a feasible returned point or start
claims.infeasible_or_unbounded: native claim that one of the two holds (claimed)
claims.none: no claim; evidence.refuted names an optimal status that failed its re-check
claims.numerical_optimum: native optimal status; the candidate is re-evaluated (objective, bounds, constraints, integrality) and an LP's duals pass the KKT acceptance; numerical, not an exact certificate
claims.unbounded: native unboundedness claim (claimed); a returned point is only a feasible point

evaluation.result: claim feasible within the tolerances, else none; objective, violations and objective_bounds.primal for a feasible point

examples.description: Continuous LP: maximize 3 x0 + 2 x1 subject to x0 + x1 <= 4, 2 x0 + x1 <= 5, x >= 0 (upper bounds null = +infinity); optimum 9 at [1, 3].

Binary knapsack MIP with a complete start: maximize 7 x0 + 11 x1 + 5 x2 + 6 x3 subject to 3 x0 + 5 x1 + 2 x2 + 4 x3 <= 8.5; the start [0, 1, 1, 0] (objective 16) is an incumbent candidate; optimum 18 at [1, 1, 0, 0].
Check three points of the knapsack without solving: [1, 1, 0, 0] (feasible, 18), [0, 1, 1, 0] (feasible, 16) and [1, 1, 1, 0] (row violated by 1.5).

lp-ip.model/1.$comment: Rules outside this schema, checked by the worker: n = len(objective) >= 1 and m = len(row_lower); variable_lower, variable_upper and kinds have n entries and row_upper has m; lower <= upper for every variable and row, where null means -infinity as a lower and +infinity as an upper bound (JSON has no NaN or Infinity); a binary variable needs bounds inside [0, 1]. Solver domain, reported per task as termination unsupported instead of a validation error: a MIP needs finite bounds of magnitude at most 2^53-1 on every variable, continuous ones included, after root bound inference, which runs only with presolve true. Integers are written without a fraction or exponent. scripts/mps_to_model.py converts MPS files to this format.
lp-ip.model/1.description: minimize or maximize objective_offset + objective . x subject to row_lower <= A x <= row_upper and variable_lower <= x <= variable_upper, x[j] integral where kinds[j] is integer or binary.

matrix.$comment: len(indptr) = m + 1, indptr[0] = 0, indptr never decreases and indptr[m] = len(indices) = len(values). Row r holds the entries indptr[r] up to indptr[r+1] - 1; their indices are strictly increasing (sorted, no duplicates) and below n. Explicit zeros are allowed. A model without rows uses indptr [0].
matrix.description: A in zero-based compressed sparse row (CSR) form, row-major over the m rows.

lp-ip.solve/1.$comment: Rules outside this schema: the job has exactly one input, its name equals model_input, it holds an lp-ip.model/1 artifact and its sha256 matches. resources.inner_threads must lie in 1..8 and becomes Options::threads. The worker forces component_threads, packing_workers and tree_threads to 1, sets the time limit to the remaining wall time and keeps every other native option at its default. Integers are written without a fraction or exponent.
